title: Coastal Archaeology of Britain
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.answer: B — The rising awareness of climate change.
questions.answerKey: B — The rising awareness of climate change.
questions.prompt: “What has caused public interest in coastal archaeology in recent years?”
questions.translation: 近年是甚麼引起公眾對 coastal archaeology 的興趣？

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph B第一句：
“It is possible to trace a variety of causes for this concentration of effort and interest.”
中文意思：
這種努力和興趣的集中，可以追溯到多種原因。
最後一句：

“At the same time archaeologists were beginning to recognize that the destruction caused by natural processes of coastal erosion and by human activity was having an increasing impact on the archaeological resource of the coast.”
中文意思：
同時，考古學家開始意識到 coastal erosion 的自然過程和 human activity 造成的破壞，正對海岸考古資源產生愈來愈大的影響。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph B 正在解釋為何 coastal archaeology 近年受到更多注意。題目問 caused public interest，所以本段第一句的 “causes” 和 “interest” 已經非常吻合。
用題目詞定位
題目中最有定位力的字是 “public interest” 和 “recent years”。原文不一定逐字寫 public interest，但會有 “broader public debate”、“awareness” 這類詞。
原文關鍵句：
“In the 1980s and 1990s scientific research into climate change and its environmental impact spilled over into a much broader public debate as awareness of these issues grew…”
中文意思：
在 1980s 和 1990s，關於 climate change 及其 environmental impact 的科學研究，隨著人們對這些議題的意識增加，擴展成更廣泛的 public debate。
細讀答案句

這句的主語是 “scientific research into climate change and its environmental impact”。核心動作是 “spilled over into a much broader public debate”。這表示本來是科學研究的議題，後來進入大眾討論。題目問 public interest 的原因，原文給出的原因正是 climate change awareness grew。
選項 B “The rising awareness of climate change” 對應原文 “awareness of these issues grew”，而 “these issues” 指前面的 climate change and environmental impact。
錯項排除： A “rapid development of England’s coastal archaeology” 太籠統。Paragraph A 說 recognition 是important development，但 Question 14 問 public interest 的原因。
C “discovery of an underwater forest” 對應 submerged forests，但那是 long been known，不是recent public interest 的主因。
D “systematic research” 在 Paragraph A 出現，但原文說 serious attention since early 1980s，並未說它引起 public interest。
public interest = broader public debate rising awareness = awareness grew climate change = climate change and its environmental impact所以答案是 B。

questions.answer: C — There is a gap of one thousand years in the record of boat use.
questions.answerKey: C — There is a gap of one thousand years in the record of boat use.
questions.prompt: “What does the passage say about the evidence of boats?”
questions.translation: 文章對 boats 的證據說了甚麼？

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph F第一句：
“The most striking evidence for use of the sea is in the form of boats, yet we still have much to learn about their production and use.”
中文意思：
人類使用海洋最突出的證據是 boats，但我們對它們的製作和使用仍有很多需要了解。
最後一句：

“Boats were some of the most complex artefacts produced by pre-modern societies, and further research on their production and use would make an important contribution to our understanding of past attitudes to technology and technological change.”
中文意思：
Boats 是 pre-modern societies 製作過的最複雜 artefacts 之一，進一步研究它們的製作和使用，會大大幫助我們理解過去人們對 technology 和 technological change 的態度。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph F 是 boat evidence 段。題目直接問 evidence of boats，所以此段是最直接目標。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “boats”。掃描 Paragraph F，最有答案價值的是有明確時間和 gap 的句子：

“The prehistoric sewn-plank boats such as those from the Humber estuary and Dover all seem to belong to the second millennium BC; after this, there is an unexplained gap of a millennium before boats reappear, built using a very different technology.”
中文意思：
Humber estuary 和 Dover 等地的 prehistoric sewn-plank boats 似乎都屬於公元前第二個千年；在此之後，記錄中出現一個無法解釋的千年缺口，然後 boats 才再次出現，而且使用了非常不同的技術建造。
細讀答案句
這句有兩個時間層次。第一，某些 prehistoric sewn-plank boats 屬於 second millennium BC。第二，after this 有 “an unexplained gap of a millennium”。a millennium 就是一千年。題目選項 C 說

“There is a gap of one thousand years in the record of boat use”，這正好對應 “an unexplained gap of a millennium before boats reappear”。錯項排除： A 說我們已經有足夠 prehistoric boatbuilding knowledge，但原文第一句說 “we still have much to learn”，方向相反。 B 說 many boats were found in harbours，原文只說 known wrecks around our coast 多屬post-medieval，沒有說多數在 harbours。 D 說 boats were first used for fishing，文章沒有提供這個起源用途。
one thousand years = a millennium gap in the record = unexplained gap before boats reappear boat use = production and use / boats reappear所以答案是 C。

questions.prompt: “What can be discovered from the air?”

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph H第一句：
“One of the most important revelations of recent research has been the extent of industrial activity along the coast.”
中文意思：
近期研究最重要的發現之一，是沿海工業活動的範圍。
最後一句：
“These industries are poorly documented, but their remains are sometimes extensive and striking.”
中文意思：
這些工業的文獻記錄不足，但它們的遺跡有時範圍很廣，而且很醒目。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph H 會講 coastal industries 的考古證據。題目問 from the air，應尋找 aerial photographs、air surveys 一類字眼。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “from the air”。原文中的直接對應是 “visible in aerial photographs”。
原文關鍵句：
“Elaborate wooden fish weirs, often of considerable extent and visible in aerial photographs of shallow water, have been identified in areas such as Essex and the Severn estuary.”
中文意思：
精巧的 wooden fish weirs 往往範圍相當大，並可在 shallow water 的 aerial photographs 中看見；它們已在 Essex 和 Severn estuary 等地被辨認出來。
細讀答案句

“aerial photographs” 即從空中拍攝的照片。從這些照片中可見的是 “Elaborate wooden fish weirs”。Fish weirs 是捕魚設施，屬於 fishing / fisheries 的考古證據。選項 D “Fisheries” 是對 fish weirs 的概括。錯項排除： A salt mines：同段有 salt production，但沒有說從空中可見。 B Roman towns：Paragraph G 提到 Roman and medieval towns 的 waterfront archaeology，但沒有 aerial photographs。 C harbours：Paragraph G 提到 harbours，但題目 “from the air” 的證據在 Paragraph H 的 fish weirs。
from the air = aerial photographs fisheries = fish weirs / facilities for procuring fish and shellfish discovered = identified所以答案是 D。

questions.prompt: “England lost a large area of land after the Ice Age because sea level rose.”
questions.translation: Ice Age 後，由於海平面上升，England 失去了大片土地。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph C第一句：
“The dominant process affecting the physical form of England in the post-glacial period has been the rise in sea level relative to the land, as the glaciers melted and the landmass readjusted.”
中文意思：
在 post-glacial period，影響 England physical form 的主導過程，是冰川融化和陸塊重新調整後，海平面相對於土地上升。
最後一句：
“The detailed reconstruction of coastline histories and the changing environments available for human use will be an important theme for future research.”
中文意思：
詳細重建 coastline histories 和可供人類使用的 changing environments，將會是 future research的重要主題。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph C 講海平面上升如何改變 England 的地形和 coast。題目有after Ice Age、sea level rose、lost land，全部和本段主題吻合。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “lost a large area of land” 和 “sea level rose”。原文中可找到：
“The encroachment of the sea, the loss of huge areas of land now under the North Sea and the English Channel…”
中文意思：
海洋的侵入，以及如今位於 North Sea 和 English Channel 之下的大片土地流失……
細讀答案句
原文前一句先交代原因：“rise in sea level relative to the land”。下一句交代結果：“loss of huge areas of land”。題目說 “because sea level rose”，正是把第一句的原因放入題目。題目說 “after the Ice Age”，原文對應 “post-glacial period”，即冰後期。

after the Ice Age = post-glacial period sea level rose = rise in sea level relative to the land lost a large area of land = loss of huge areas of land England = physical form of England / land now under North Sea and English Channel題目與原文方向一致，所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “The coastline of England has changed periodically.”
questions.translation: England 的 coastline 曾按間歇或週期方式改變。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph C第一句：
“The dominant process affecting the physical form of England in the post-glacial period has been the rise in sea level relative to the land, as the glaciers melted and the landmass readjusted.”
中文意思：
在冰後期，影響 England physical form 的主導過程，是海平面相對於土地上升。
最後一句：
“The detailed reconstruction of coastline histories and the changing environments available for human use will be an important theme for future research.”
中文意思：
詳細重建 coastline histories 和可供人類使用的 changing environments，將會是未來研究的重要主題。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph C 會講海岸線和環境如何改變。題目中的 coastline changed相關，但 “periodically” 是真正要檢查的控制詞。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “coastline” 和 “periodically”。原文沒有 periodically，但有：
“we know little about the constant reconfiguration of the coastline.”
中文意思：
我們對 coastline 的持續重組所知甚少。
細讀答案句
原文用的是 “constant reconfiguration”。constant 表示持續不斷；reconfiguration 表示形狀或配置被重新組合。題目說 “periodically”，意思偏向按間隔、間歇或週期發生。這裡的頻率概念不同：原文強調 constant，題目改成 periodically，會改變原文意思。
這題不能只看 “coastline has changed”。文章確實說 coastline 有 reconfiguration，但題目加入了
“periodically” 這個方式。原文提供的是 constant reconfiguration，沒有支持 periodical change；更準確地說，原文的頻率訊號和題目不一致。
coastline changed = reconfiguration of the coastline periodically = at intervals / from time to time constant = continuous / ongoing因為題目中的改變方式和原文的 constant reconfiguration 不一致，所以答案是 FALSE。

questions.prompt: “Coastal archaeological evidence may be well preserved by its physical environment.”
questions.translation: Coastal archaeological evidence 可能因其 physical environment 而保存良好。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph D第一句：

“So great has been the rise in sea level and the consequent regression of the coast that much of the archaeological evidence now exposed in the coastal zone, whether being eroded or revealed as a buried land surface, derives from what was originally terrestrial occupation.”
中文意思：
海平面上升和海岸後退的程度很大，因此今天在 coastal zone 暴露出來的許多 archaeological evidence，無論正被侵蝕，或作為 buried land surface 被揭示，都來自原本的陸地居住活動。
最後一句：
“Nevertheless, its physical environment means that preservation is often excellent, for example in the case of the Neolithic structure excavated at the Stumble in Essex.”
中文意思：
然而，它的 physical environment 意味著保存狀況往往非常好，例如 Essex 的 Stumble 出土的Neolithic structure。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph D 說明某些 coastal evidence 原本是 terrestrial occupation，但在 coastal zone 中保存很好。題目中 physical environment 和 well preserved 明顯對應本段最後一句。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “physical environment” 和 “well preserved”。原文直接有：
“its physical environment means that preservation is often excellent”
這句同時包含 physical environment 和 preservation，因此值得細讀。
細讀答案句
原文說 “preservation is often excellent”，意思是保存通常很好。題目說 “may be well preserved”，語氣較保守。原文的 often excellent 完全足以支持 may be well preserved。
may be = often can be / often is well preserved = preservation is often excellent by its physical environment = its physical environment means that題目與原文一致，所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “Boats made by pre-modern societies were very simple in design.”
questions.translation: Pre-modern societies 製造的 boats 設計非常簡單。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph F第一句：
“The most striking evidence for use of the sea is in the form of boats, yet we still have much to learn about their production and use.”
中文意思：
使用海洋最突出的證據是 boats，但我們對它們的製作和使用仍有很多需要了解。
最後一句：

“Boats were some of the most complex artefacts produced by pre-modern societies, and further research on their production and use would make an important contribution to our understanding of past attitudes to technology and technological change.”
中文意思：
Boats 是 pre-modern societies 製作過的最複雜 artefacts 之一，進一步研究它們的製作和使用，會大大幫助我們理解過去人們對技術和技術變化的態度。
只看首尾句，Paragraph F 直接提到 pre-modern societies 和 boats 的 complexity。題目說simple in design，這和最後一句形成強烈對比。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “pre-modern societies” 和 “simple in design”。原文出現：
“some of the most complex artefacts produced by pre-modern societies”
細讀答案句
原文說 boats 是 “some of the most complex artefacts”，也就是最複雜的 artefacts 之一。題目說
“very simple in design”，和 complex 方向相反。
very simple in design = not complex most complex artefacts = highly complex objects made by pre-modern societies = produced by pre-modern societies題目與原文清楚相衝，所以答案是 FALSE。

questions.prompt: “Similar boats were also discovered in many other European countries.”
questions.translation: 在許多其他 European countries 也發現了類似 boats。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph F第一句：
“The most striking evidence for use of the sea is in the form of boats, yet we still have much to learn about their production and use.”
中文意思：
使用海洋最突出的證據是 boats，但我們對它們的製作和使用仍有很多需要了解。
最後一句：

“Boats were some of the most complex artefacts produced by pre-modern societies, and further research on their production and use would make an important contribution to our understanding of past attitudes to technology and technological change.”
中文意思：
Boats 是 pre-modern societies 製作過的最複雜 artefacts 之一，進一步研究它們的製作和使用，會幫助我們理解過去對技術和技術變化的態度。
本段講 boats evidence，但題目加入 “many other European countries”，所以要尋找是否有跨國發現資料。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “similar boats”、“many other European countries”。Paragraph F 提到地點：
“the Humber estuary and Dover”
也提到 “around our coast”，但沒有提到 many European countries。
細讀證據是否足夠
原文說：
“The prehistoric sewn-plank boats such as those from the Humber estuary and Dover all seem to belong to the second millennium BC…”
中文意思：
Humber estuary 和 Dover 等地的 prehistoric sewn-plank boats 似乎都屬於公元前第二個千年。
這句只提供英國範圍內的例子。文章沒有說歐洲其他國家也發現 similar boats，也沒有說沒有發現。題目需要 “many other European countries” 這個地理範圍；原文缺少這個範圍資料。
因此答案是 NOT GIVEN。
“Humber estuary and Dover” 都是地名，容易讓人以為文章在列舉多國例子。細讀後會見到它們仍屬英國 coastal evidence 的語境，未建立 “many other European countries” 的資訊。

questions.prompt: “There are few documents relating to mineral exploitation.”
questions.translation: 關於 mineral exploitation 的文件記錄很少。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph H第一句：
“One of the most important revelations of recent research has been the extent of industrial activity along the coast.”
中文意思：
近期研究最重要的發現之一，是沿海 industrial activity 的範圍。
最後一句：
“These industries are poorly documented, but their remains are sometimes extensive and striking.”
中文意思：
這些 industries 的文獻記錄不足，但它們的遺跡有時範圍很大，也很醒目。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph H 講 coastal industries 及其 archaeological remains。題目提到 mineral exploitation，所以要看本段後半列出的 mineral resources。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “mineral exploitation”。原文有：
“mineral resources such as sand, gravel, stone, coal, ironstone, and alum were all exploited.”
中文意思：
sand、gravel、stone、coal、ironstone 和 alum 等 mineral resources 全都曾被開採利用。
緊接著：
“These industries are poorly documented…”
中文意思：
這些 industries 的文獻記錄不足。
細讀答案句
“These industries” 指前面列出的 coastal industries，包括 mineral resources exploitation。題目說 “few documents”，原文說 “poorly documented”。兩者意思一致，都是文獻資料少、記錄不足。
few documents = poorly documented mineral exploitation = mineral resources … were all exploited relating to = these industries題目和原文一致，所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “Large passenger ferries are causing increasing damage to the shore.”
questions.translation: 大型 passenger ferries 正對海岸造成愈來愈大的損害。

blocks.text: 先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph I第一句：

“Some appreciation of the variety and importance of the archaeological remains preserved in the coastal zone, albeit only in preliminary form, can thus be gained from recent work, but the complexity of the problem of managing that resource is also being realized.”
中文意思：
近期研究讓人初步認識 coastal zone 中保存的 archaeological remains 的多樣性和重要性，但人們也開始意識到管理這項資源的問題很複雜。
最後一句：

“The management of the archaeological remains will have to be considered over a much longer timescale and a much wider geographical scale than is common in the case of dry land sites, and this will pose a serious challenge for archaeologists.”
中文意思：
管理這些 archaeological remains 時，需要比 dry land sites 採用更長的時間尺度和更大的地理尺度，這會對 archaeologists 構成嚴重挑戰。
只看首尾句，可以估計 Paragraph I 講 coastal archaeological remains 的管理和 threats。題目提到 ferries damage，所以要在本段中找 human threats。
用題目詞定位
題目定位詞是 “ferries” 和 “damage”。原文直接有：
“The larger size of ferries has also caused an increase in the damage caused by their wash to fragile deposits in the intertidal zone.”
中文意思：
ferries 尺寸變大，也使它們的 wash 對 intertidal zone 中 fragile deposits 造成的破壞增加。
細讀答案句
題目說 “Large passenger ferries”。原文說 “larger size of ferries”。雖然原文沒有 passenger 一字，但 ferries 通常是載人或車輛渡輪；題目的核心是 size of ferries and damage。原文清楚說larger ferries caused an increase in damage。
“wash” 指船行駛時造成的水浪。這些水浪損害 intertidal zone 的 fragile deposits，也就是海岸潮間帶的脆弱沉積物。題目的 “shore” 是對 intertidal zone 的概括。
large ferries = larger size of ferries causing increasing damage = caused an increase in the damage shore = intertidal zone / coastal fragile deposits題目與原文一致，所以答案是 TRUE。

questions.prompt: “Which THREE of the following statements are mentioned in the passage?”
questions.translation: 以下哪三項在文章中有提及？

blocks.text: 這類 Multiple-answer Questions 要逐項獨立證明，不能用模糊段落一次包辦幾個答案。手冊也提醒，Choose TWO / THREE 題要追蹤每個選項是否被提及、支持、限制或否定。
選項 B B：It is difficult to understand how many people lived close to the sea.
很難知道有多少人住在海邊附近。
先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph E第一句：
“In some cases these buried land surfaces do contain evidence for human exploitation of what was a coastal environment, and elsewhere along the modern coast there is similar evidence.”
中文意思：
在某些情況下，這些 buried land surfaces 確實包含人類利用 coastal environment 的證據；在現代海岸其他地方，也有類似證據。
最後一句：

“We are not yet in a position to give even preliminary answers to such fundamental questions as the extent to which the sea and the coast affected human life in the past, what percentage of the population at any time lived within reach of the sea, or whether human settlements in coastal environments showed a distinct character from those inland.”
中文意思：
我們甚至還未能對一些基本問題給出初步答案，例如過去 sea and coast 在多大程度上影響人類生活、任何時期有多少人口比例住在可接近海洋的範圍內，或 coastal environments 中的人類聚落是否有別於 inland 聚落。
原文說 “not yet in a position to give even preliminary answers”，即連初步答案都未能提供。接著其中一個問題正是 “what percentage of the population at any time lived within reach of the sea”。這直接對應選項 B。
difficult to understand = not yet in a position to give even preliminary answers how many people = what percentage of the population lived close to the sea = lived within reach of the sea所以 B 有提及。
選項 D D：Our knowledge of archaeological evidence relating to boats is limited.
中文意思：
我們對 boats 相關 archaeological evidence 的認識有限。
先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph F第一句：
“The most striking evidence for use of the sea is in the form of boats, yet we still have much to learn about their production and use.”
中文意思：
人類使用海洋最突出的證據是 boats，但我們對其製作和使用仍有很多需要了解。
最後一句：

“Boats were some of the most complex artefacts produced by pre-modern societies, and further research on their production and use would make an important contribution to our understanding of past attitudes to technology and technological change.”
中文意思：
Boats 是 pre-modern societies 製作過的最複雜 artefacts 之一，進一步研究它們的製作和使用，會大大幫助我們理解過去對技術和技術變化的態度。
原文第一句已說 “we still have much to learn”。同段又說 “Boatbuilding must have been an extremely important activity around much of our coast, yet we know almost nothing about it.”
中文意思：
Boatbuilding 必定曾是我們很多海岸地區極重要的活動，但我們幾乎對它一無所知。
這些句子直接支持 D。
knowledge is limited = still have much to learn / know almost nothing archaeological evidence relating to boats = evidence for use of the sea is in the form of boats所以 D 有提及。
選項 F F：Human development threatens archaeological remains.
中文意思：
人類發展威脅 archaeological remains。
先看段落功能
目標段落：Paragraph I第一句：

“Some appreciation of the variety and importance of the archaeological remains preserved in the coastal zone, albeit only in preliminary form, can thus be gained from recent work, but the complexity of the problem of managing that resource is also being realized.”
中文意思：
近期研究讓人初步認識 coastal zone 中 archaeological remains 的多樣性和重要性，但人們也開始意識到管理這項資源的問題很複雜。
最後一句：

“The management of the archaeological remains will have to be considered over a much longer timescale and a much wider geographical scale than is common in the case of dry land sites, and this will pose a serious challenge for archaeologists.”
中文意思：
管理這些 archaeological remains 時，需要比 dry land sites 採用更長時間尺度和更大地理尺度，這會對 archaeologists 構成嚴重挑戰。
原文中間明確說：

“Human threats include the redevelopment of historic towns and old dockland areas, and the increased importance of the coast for the leisure and tourism industries, resulting in pressure for the increased provision of facilities such as marinas.”
中文意思：
Human threats 包括 historic towns 和 old dockland areas 的 redevelopment，以及海岸對leisure and tourism industries 變得更重要，因而帶來更多 marinas 等設施的建設壓力。
這直接支持 F。Human development 包括 redevelopment、tourism facilities、marinas 等，這些都威脅 coastal archaeological resource。

human development = redevelopment / increased provision of facilities threatens = human threats include archaeological remains = archaeological remains preserved in the coastal zone / resource所以 F 有提及。
其餘選項排除A “How coastal archaeology was originally discovered” Paragraph A 說 submerged forests 很早吸引 antiquarians，serious attention 到 1980s 才出現，但沒有交代 coastal archaeology 如何「最初被發現」的過程。A 範圍過大。
C “The extent to which prehistoric communities understood climate change” Paragraph C 討論 prehistoric communities 如何 adjusted to environmental changes，但沒有說他們是否理解 climate change，也沒有談 understanding 的程度。
E “Some former fishing grounds were converted into ports”文章分別提到 fishing evidence 和 ports / harbours / landing places，但沒有說 former fishing grounds 被 converted into ports。

G “Coastal archaeology will become more important in the future”文章說 future research 會重視 coastline histories，也說 management 會成為 challenge，但沒有直接說 coastal archaeology 本身將變得更重要。G 把 future research 和 importance 推得太遠。
所以 Questions 24–26 答案是 B, D, F。

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：全文段落地圖
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 首句指出近年最重要的發展之一，是人們開始認識 England coastal archaeology 的 wealth and diversity。末句說 submerged forests 早於十八世紀已吸引 antiquarians，但 serious and systematic attention 到 1980s 初才出現。只看首尾句，可以估計本段是開場背景段：它先說coastal archaeology 近年受到重視，再補充其實部分資源很早已被注意，只是系統研究較晚才開始。

首句說可以追溯這股研究和興趣集中的多種原因。末句指出 archaeologists 開始意識到 coastal erosion 和 human activity 對 coast archaeological resource 的破壞愈來愈大。只看首尾句，可以估計本段在解釋「為何近年突然重視 coastal archaeology」。中間提到 climate change、rising sea levels 和 public debate，因此 Question 14 很大機會在此段定位。

首句說 post-glacial period 影響 England physical form 的主導過程，是相對於土地的 sea level rise。末句說 reconstructing coastline histories 和 changing environments 會成為 future research的重要主題。只看首尾句，可以估計本段講冰後期海平面上升、土地流失、海岸線重組，以及prehistoric communities 如何適應這些環境變化。Questions 17–18 會在這段檢查。

首句說 sea level rise 和 coast regression 很大，以致今日 coastal zone 暴露的考古證據，很多原本來自 terrestrial occupation。末句以 Essex 的 Stumble Neolithic structure 為例，說 physical environment 令保存狀況常常 excellent。只看首尾句，可以估計本段提醒讀者：有些 coastal evidence 原本不是海岸生活證據，但因保存良好仍很有價值。Question 19 會看這段。

首句說某些 buried land surfaces 確實包含人類利用 coastal environment 的證據。末句說研究者仍無法初步回答一些基本問題，例如過去多少人口住在 sea 附近，或 coastal settlements 是否有別於 inland settlements。只看首尾句，可以估計本段重點是 coastal exploitation evidence 很多元，但理解仍很有限。Question 24–26 的 B 很可能來自這段。

首句說最明顯的 sea use evidence 是 boats，但研究者對其製作和使用仍有很多未明。末句說進一步研究 boats 的 production and use，可大大幫助理解 past attitudes to technology and technological change。只看首尾句，可以估計本段集中於船隻證據、wrecks、prehistoric sewn-plank boats、一千年記錄缺口，以及 pre-modern boats 的技術複雜性。Questions 15、20、21 和 D 都指向此段。

首句說 boats need landing places，但我們對 landing places 的認識也很零碎。末句說redevelopment、development 和 natural pressures 正令這些重要地點面臨 unprecedented threats，但相關 surveys 很少。只看首尾句，可以估計本段處理 ports、harbours、quays、wharves、jetties 等登岸設施，以及小型 landing places 研究不足和受威脅的問題。

首句說 recent research 的重大發現之一，是 coast 沿線 industrial activity 的 extent。末句說其他coastal industries 文獻記錄不足，但遺跡有時 extensive and striking。只看首尾句，可以估計本段介紹 coastal industry evidence，包括 fishing、salt production、fish weirs、mineral resources。 Question 16 的 aerial photographs、Question 22 的 poorly documented 都在這段。

首句說 recent work 讓人初步欣賞 coastal zone 遺跡的 variety and importance，同時也意識到management problem 很複雜。末句說 coastal archaeological remains 的管理需要比 dry land sites 更長時間尺度和更大地理尺度，這對 archaeologists 會是 serious challenge。只看首尾句，可以估計本段是總結管理段：它列出 human threats、natural threats、sea-level rise、ferries damage 和保護困難。Question 23 和 F 會定位到這裡。
